name: glycolysis_coupled
description: Arm 6 (coupling demonstration): arm 3's modular glycolysis decomposition with the lower-glycolysis submodel swapped for a NATIVE process-bigraph process (hand-ported Teusink RHS + scipy) while upper glycolysis stays a Tellurium/libroadrunner submodel — two different simulation engines sharing one species store and reconciling additively. A composition a single monolithic SBML/libroadrunner model structurally cannot express (it solves the same ODEs, reproducing arm 3 to ~1e-7; the impossibility is structural, not numeric), and which is kept off the accuracy axis as the composability existence proof.

upper_glycolysis.doc:
One biological submodel as a standalone bigraph process node.

Holds a single libroadrunner instance built from the SAME model but keeping
only ``reactions`` (all species, parameters and assignment rules retained).
Each ``update(interval)`` reads the shared settable species from the store,
advances this submodel's reactions over ``interval``, and returns the **delta**
it produced on the settable species. Because the store's ``map[float]`` applies
numeric updates additively, the deltas of all submodel nodes reconcile by
summation through the bigraph apply path.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

lower_glycolysis.doc:
One native-pbg reaction SUBMODEL as a bigraph process node (arm 6).

The native analogue of arm 3's :class:`SubmodelProcess`: it reads the shared
``species`` store, integrates ONLY its ``reactions`` subset of the native
Teusink RHS over the coupling ``interval`` with scipy, and returns the
per-species **delta** it produced. The species leaf is ``map[float]`` (NOT
overwrite), so the delta reconciles additively through the bigraph apply path
with the *other* submodel node's delta — even though that other node is a
Tellurium/libroadrunner :class:`SubmodelProcess` and this one is hand-written
Python. That cross-engine, store-coupled composition is exactly what a single
monolithic libroadrunner model cannot express.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

energy.doc:
Assignment-rule node: re-derive ATP/ADP/AMP from the reconciled pool.

Reads the shared species store after the submodel deltas have reconciled and
writes the delta that lands ``ATP``/``ADP``/``AMP`` on the values the SBML
assignment rules give for the current settable phosphate pool (``P`` and the
conserved ``SUM_P``). Only this node writes the assignment-rule species, so
there is no double counting.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
